players.product: Hong Kong carrier-neutral colocation data centres (iAdvantage MEGA Campus: MEGA-i connectivity hub, MEGA IDC high-density, liquid-cooling-ready AI campus)

quarterly_data.signal: Customers, suppliers and half-year trend (annual report): the five largest customers (including the SHKP Group) accounted for about 53% of FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) revenue and the largest about 19%; the five largest suppliers (including the SHKP Group) about 37% of total purchases and the largest about 20%. Revenue for January-June 2026 was HK$1,609,247 thousand versus HK$1,507,927 thousand for July-December 2025, and data centre business EBITDA HK$1,210,686 thousand versus HK$1,108,749 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: five largest customers about 53%, largest about 19%; five largest suppliers about 37%, largest about 20%; Jan-Jun 2026 revenue HK$1,609,247 thousand (Jul-Dec 2025: HK$1,507,927 thousand)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 operating detail (annual report): operating profit rose 9% to HK$1,631 million; total operating costs rose 3% to HK$1,497 million on higher data-centre depreciation and expansion; finance costs fell 24% to HK$256 million; net cash generated from operating activities excluding working-capital movement rose 9% to HK$2,240 million. ELV and IT systems revenue rose 5% to HK$229 million, and Super e-Technology secured ELV and IT system installation contracts totalling HK$107 million during the year. Capital expenditure contracted for but not provided for construction in progress was HK$932,825 thousand at 30 June 2026 (2025: HK$1,172,631 thousand); an independent valuer assessed the fair market value of the data centres in operation at HK$51.5 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: operating profit HK$1,631 million (+9%); ELV and IT contracts secured HK$107 million; contracted capex HK$932,825 thousand; data centres valued at HK$51.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio (annual report): data centres in operation total 2.3 million sq ft of GFA - MEGA-i (Chai Wan, 350k sq ft, in service since 2001), MEGA Two (Sha Tin, 429k), MEGA Plus (Tseung Kwan O, 474k), MEGA Fanling (129k, fully committed to a single cloud customer, asset-light), MEGA Gateway (Tsuen Wan, 201k) and MEGA IDC Phase 1 (Tseung Kwan O, ~500k, in service 2024, purpose-built for high-density / AI deployments), with future MEGA IDC phases of ~700k sq ft fast-tracked as an integrated development, plus two carrier-neutral cable landing stations, HKIS-1 and HKIS-2. The company says MEGA-i ranks among the top five connectivity hubs globally. Chairman Kwok Ping-luen, Raymond: over 50% of China's overseas internet traffic goes through Hong Kong, and China selling 'AI tokens overseas' has to be supported by sufficient subsea cable capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: 2.3 million sq ft GFA in operation; MEGA IDC Phase 1 ~500k sq ft; future phases ~700k sq ft

quarterly_data.signal: Legal (chairman's statement): following the company's successful judicial review concerning the Court of Appeal's findings that Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP) had misconstrued its policy when assessing lease compliance by its grantee data centre operators at the Tseung Kwan O InnoPark, SUNeVision continues to call on HKSTP to take enforcement action; HKCOLO.NET Limited is the subject of enforcement proceedings by HKSTP for repossession of its leased land at the InnoPark, and HKCOLO.NET has initiated defamation proceedings against the group, which maintains its statements were fair and accurate, rejects the allegations and will defend the proceedings robustly.
